chose: a moved sink is re-addressed by MATCHED DISAPPEARANCE: an unmatched site inherits a baselined review only if a site with the same context|expr vanished, one for one
over: content-addressed keys (drop the path from identity entirely) — cheapest and it fixes the reported symptom, but it converts 'a NEW raw site fails' into 'a new raw EXPRESSION fails': a reviewed ${row.name} could then be copy-pasted into fifty new and more dangerous files for free. The ratchet's whole value is site-level, so this buys quiet at the price of the thing it protects

git-rename-aware reconciliation (--find-renames / log --follow) — most precise, but it makes a tree-reading ratchet depend on VCS history: shallow CI clones, non-git consumers, and uncommitted working-tree moves (exactly when CI runs --check) all break it, and it still misses a move done as copy-then-delete
basename-only or path-normalized keys — still breaks on a rename and collides across same-named files (index.ts everywhere); strictly worse than either real option
keep failing on a move but with a friendlier message — the incident is that the alarm was DISBELIEVED, and a better-worded false alarm is still a false alarm
because: a ratchet baseline is a cached review, and a cached fact that expires on a rename is premise rot one layer down. Keying by path made a refactor manufacture false security alarms in proportion to how much code it moved (hoist: 4 of 7 reported 'new' sites were untouched). Conservation of count per context|expr is what keeps the loosening honest — relocation changes WHERE a reviewed site lives, duplication changes HOW MUCH unreviewed surface exists, and only the second is news

chose: the false-negative the fix ACCEPTS: a sink that moved into a genuinely more exposed file no longer fails --check; it is reported by name, from → to, instead
over: gating on the move as well (fail --check on any relocation) — that is the status quo and the reason the ratchet got disbelieved
gating only on moves that cross a component boundary — needs a notion of 'more exposed' the sinks lint does not have, and would fire on every extraction refactor, which is the exact case that broke
because: the sink CONTEXT (sql-ident vs html-value) is still part of the address, so a move that changes the KIND of sink is novel and does fail. What is given up is path-level exposure judgment, which the lint never actually had — it only ever knew that a path string changed. Moving the fact from silent to READ (an explicit MOVED block with old → new) is the honest rung on the price ladder for something the tool cannot decide

chose: when several byte-identical sites share one context|expr, WHICH new path inherits which vanished review is arbitrary — a test that asserted the moved site by path passed only by walk order (render.ts sorting before tools.ts), and flipped when a third file was added
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
the pairing is genuinely under-determined and only the COUNT is a real guarantee — attribution is cosmetic and the report's from → to line can name the wrong 'from' when duplicates exist
a nearest-path heuristic (longest shared directory prefix) would recover the intended pairing in nearly every real refactor, making the reported from → to trustworthy rather than merely deterministic
discriminatedBy: replay hoist's actual eight-subsystem extraction through reconcile and check whether any context|expr had >1 vanished site; if none did, the ambiguity never fires in practice and the heuristic buys nothing. If some did, compare sorted-order pairing against longest-common-prefix pairing on the real git rename map

chose: left conventions.ts unchanged — its baseline is name-keyed and is already move-immune
over: applying the same matched-disappearance reconciliation to the conventions ratchet for symmetry
because: measured it, did not assume: baselined a guard at 2 call sites, then moved BOTH its declaration and a call site into a new subsystem dir. Ratchet stayed green. The key is {name, sites} and callSites() counts matches across the whole source set regardless of which file they live in, so relocation is invisible to it by construction. Its real sensitivity is fan-out GROWTH, which is signal, not noise — an extraction that genuinely adds call sites should fire. Symmetry is not a reason to add machinery to a component that does not have the defect
